utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Next week we might have a 92 bis witness, but up to now we are not sure whether he could come or not because the Prosecution requested the cross-examination of that 92 bis witness. As for another witness, yesterday we received some notice from the embassy that the proper paper was served to him, but he was just after an operation and could not make it. So we might arrange it sometime later, maybe during Mr. Jokic's case. It depends on the condition of his health. It is our intention to finish the testimony of this witness in three sessions this morning, because this courtroom will be used by another case. And if we couldn't finish this witness, we'll do our best, do our best to see whether there is any other courtrooms available this afternoon. Well, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any protective measures for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, there are not, and I don't anticipate this taking more than a session, actually, perhaps for both sides. But that's -- I mean, I certainly don't think I'm going to be with the witness more than an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Judge Vassylenko. Examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Can you hear me? All right. Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Good. Could you please tell us your name.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Nikola Popovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell us your last name letter by letter.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: P-o-p-o-v-i-c, diacritic. N-i-k-o-l-a.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popovic. Now, back in July 1995, were you a member of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how you were serving in the brigade, in what capacity.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I was a military policeman of the Bratunac Brigade, and my duty was to carry out police work in the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did there come a time last year when you learned through the press what Momir Nikolic had stated about you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what you had heard Momir Nikolic had stated.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I read about it. It was in the newspaper, a newspaper called Blic. And I read that he had accused me and four of my neighbours from Kravica of crimes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, just to be precise on this, I want to put on the ELMO exactly what Momir Nikolic had stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I could have the assistance of the usher. I'm going to be reading from P82, Prosecution Exhibit P82. It would be on page 5, sir. Mr. Usher, if you could -- page 5, and towards the latter part of the page, the paragraph where it starts with: "I established."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to read this part, Mr. Popovic, very slowly for you to listen, and then I will ask you some questions. According to Mr. Nikolic, when he gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecution - and this would have been, to have the exact date, I believe it was June -- or May, May 6th, 2003 - he said: "I established that among those participating in the executions were Nikola Popovic, from Kravica, who was attached to the Bratunac Brigade Military Police, Milovan Matic, who was attached to the 1st Infantry Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade; Ilija Nikolic, who was attached to the 1st Infantry Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade; Raso Milanovic, who was the commander of the Police Unit in Kravica." And if we go to the -- further up in that -- in the same page, Mr. Nikolic is referring to the executions that occurred at the Kravica warehouse. Concretely, Mr. Popovic, did you participate in any executions at the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Among my relatives, two members of my family were killed and two members of my wife's family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe you didn't hear my question. I'm asking you concretely whether you participated in any executions at the Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure about that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't there at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, then, why would Momir Nikolic state that you were among those others having participated at those executions?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I think that he mentioned those people because each one of us had lost family members, all the five of us whom he listed. Two members of my family were killed and also two members of my wife's family. Milovan Matic lost a brother; Ilija Nikolic also lost a brother; Jovan Nikolic also lost a brother; Raso Milanovic lost a brother who was shot in the head. And I think that he just mentioned those of us who had had a tragedy in our family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, where are you from originally?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I'm from Kravica, near Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which family members did you lose?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I lost my father, who was imprisoned on the 7th of January, 1993 in Kravica, and after that he was killed in Srebrenica a month later. I also lost my grandfather, who was slaughtered in front of his house, and his arm was cut off at the shoulder. My wife lost her mother and her sister-in-law, who was pregnant. She was seven months pregnant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: And she was 20 years old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, did you ever have a visit or a contact from members of Momir Nikolic's Defence team?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they came to my home. It was in late February or early March. Two unknown men turned up and introduced themselves as Momir Nikolic's counsel. They asked me if I knew him, and I said I did. They asked me if I knew where he was. I said I knew he was in The Hague. And then they asked me to be a witness in Nikolic's defence, and they talked to me. I refused this. I said I had family obligations, I had to work, support my family, I didn't have time to go and testify. After this, they left and they never turned up again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this visit by Nikolic's Defence team requesting that you be a witness for Momir Nikolic in this trial, was this before or after you read what Nikolic had told the Prosecutors about you and the others?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Before. Before. This was in February or March. Nobody arrived in May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, after -- after it was published, what Momir Nikolic had stated about you and the others, did you give a statement to the Bratunac police?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you what we will be marking as D205 for identification. And we have an English version as well for the ELMO. Do you recognise what I am handing you, sir?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the date of this statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: The date?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may find it on the first page.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: The 28th of August, 2003. That's when I gave the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I -- we don't need to go through the statement at this point. But just to ask you about it: When you gave a statement to the police, were you questioned about your activities surrounding the fall of Srebrenica and particularly the accusations that Momir Nikolic had lodged against you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you tell the police the same thing that you've told us under oath, and that is that you were not involved in any executions at the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Incidentally, just so we clear the air on this one, have you been involved in any atrocities during that period?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before we talk about those days, first tell us a little bit about yourself. You told us that you're from Kravica. Where did you --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: From Kravica, near Bratunac. I was mobilised in 1992, even though I was a minor. Before the war, I worked in a private bakery. And when the war began, a military bakery was set up, and this is where I worked until the fall of Kravica in 1993. And that's how I served in the army, as a baker. After the fall of Kravica in 1993, in the 1st Battalion, together with my fellow people from Kravica I worked in the kitchen until 1995, and then I went to join the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know about what time, what month in 1995, that you became a military policeman with the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: This was in early June, late May or early June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you briefly tell us in general what your functions were or your duties were as a military police officer. And I'm speaking prior to the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It was my duty as a military policeman to arrest people who didn't want to go to the front line and bring them in. We made sure that there was no disorder in the town. We secured high-ranking officers who came to visit, secured the roads. This period just before the fall of Srebrenica, we were securing the Sase-Pribicevac road, where the high-ranking officers travelled to the first line of defence. Our task was to secure this road, which went through a wood. There were some 15 of us policemen, and we were deployed every 50 or 100 metres, and they would pass by and then come back, and we were there the whole time. In the evening, we were at the police, and then we would do the same again, and that's what we did before the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to give you as a reference date July 11th, 1995, a day that is fixed with respect to the fall of Srebrenica. So keeping that date in mind as a reference, could you please tell us if you recall what you did -- or what you were doing the day Srebrenica fell.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I was at the police on the 11th of July. Our task was to work in the town, to secure these officers who came. They were having talks in Hotel Fontana in Bratunac, and we secured the Fontana Hotel and the surrounding area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. July 12th, the next day, could you please tell us what you did.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th of July, I was off. It was our big holiday, St. Peter's Day, so I was off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, what did you do on your day off?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: We had a soccer game. Bratunac Bratstvo was to play on the town stadium in Bratunac, but because of these operations the game was played in Milici. It was a game against Bijeljina. I played for this club. I was off that day so I could go to the match, and after that I was to report to the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well -- and so you did in fact go to play in Milici on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us about what time you returned to Bratunac and about what time you reported back to the military police.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I arrived in the military police sometime between 8.00 and 9.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us when you reported back to the military police, what, if any, tasks you were given.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: On that evening, I was not given any tasks. I spent the night in the military police quarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next day, July 13th, could you please tell us what you did that day, in a chronological order.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: On that day - this was the 13th - I was deployed in Potocari. In the morning of the 13th, we were given our tasks and I was deployed in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now I want to go step by step. First of all, could you please tell us who it was that ordered you or deployed you to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly who issued the order. It was the duty officer. He read out the list of men who were to go to Potocari. It was about half of us. There were some 12 or 15 military policemen deployed in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us about what time it was that you were deployed.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: It might have been between 8.00 and 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know how you -- could you please tell us how you got to Potocari from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: We arrived in our car. We had a car, a TAM van, a military one, and a Pinz. We used the TAM to go to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Who was your komandir among you, if there was one?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: It was Mirko Jankovic from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he with you at that point in time? I know he was the commander of the military police, but do you recall whether he was with you on that particular morning, the morning of July 13, 1995?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. I do remember -- it wasn't him. No, no, it was ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, once you got to Potocari, could you please tell us what exactly you did.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: We were providing security. The UNPROFOR battalion was also there - I don't know exactly which one - but we were there together in a compound, and up above there were some soldiers wearing black overalls. I think it was some kind of special unit, and they were letting the civilians go through, and we were just securing the road to the buses. We were deployed there, and they were boarding the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall who it was that gave you that particular task?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, I don't remember. There was the patrol leader there, but I can't recall his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever ordered or did you ever engage in the separation process, that is, separating the men, military-age men, from their families?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. That was not our task. It was other soldiers who did that. The ones that they separated off, we had to put them on buses. That was the task of us military policemen. UNPROFOR was there too, and we were just securing the route from the place where they were separating people off to the buses. It might have been some 70 or 100 metres from there to where the buses were parked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you please tell us who those other soldiers were that were engaged in the separation process.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: These were soldiers belonging to some special unit. They wore a special type of clothing too, some kind of black overalls and caps and things like that, a special unit. Now, I don't know what else I can say. It was their task to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was commanding them?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. At that time, General Krstic was there, Mladic also came. He would come and go and come and go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you by any chance have any conversations with those men to find out who they were, where they were from, why they were there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't dare walk up to them, let alone talk to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we couldn't get up to them when they were above us then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that you were securing a road or securing a pathway. Could you please describe that to us. What exactly you were doing? You and the others, that is, so we have some kind of a visual picture.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, from the place where the separation took place to the bus, there was about 80 to 100 metres, and the Muslim detainees went on foot. So we were by the road, and they were walking down the asphalt road to the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever ordered by anyone to abuse any of those people, those refugees, men or women?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see whether any other members of the Bratunac Military Police were there abusing the women, the children, the men?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. No one from our unit did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us how long you were in Potocari on that day, that is, July 13, 1995.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we were there while the civilians were getting out, and then the military-age, able-bodied men started boarding the buses. I don't know exactly how many there were, say about 15. And then after that we boarded the buses, and we took the Muslim population towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. At what time did you eventually leave Potocari?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: It was around noon or, rather, 2.00 or 3.00, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And after that, where were you tasked?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: We boarded the buses, where the Muslim inhabitants were, the able-bodied ones of military age.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who ordered you to board the buses?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. This man I don't know, who was there, who was in charge, he said, "You, the military police, you provide security for these men," and they stayed back in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that man -- did you recognise that man? Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, I did not know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That wasn't Momir Nikolic, was it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you know -- from the way he was dressed, were you able to recognise whether he was an officer or just a -- a soldier, like yourself?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, it was an officer. He even had that cap, that officer's cap on his head, and he had officer's insignia, and he said, "You military police report to escort the convoy."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What -- did you say to him that -- did you ask him who he was to give you orders, since you didn't recognise him, and from that answer it would appear that he wasn't from the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, he wasn't from the Bratunac Brigade for sure. We didn't ask him anything. We did what he told us to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I guess I'm -- I'm a little lost here. If he wasn't from the Bratunac Brigade, he wasn't your komandir, he wasn't your komandant, why didn't you tell him that -- that he had no business giving you orders, that he wasn't in a position to give you orders?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we didn't dare say that, because we saw he was some kind of an officer, that he had some kind of insignia and that he was wearing an officer's uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you got to Bratunac, could you please tell us what you did that day. You said you left in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We left on those buses that were taking the Muslim people from Srebrenica. We went towards the school, to be precise, the Branko Radicevic School, I think that was the name of the school at that time. And the Muslims were put up at that school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it not seem rather strange to you that they would just be taken from Potocari and bussed just 5 kilometres away and be put in -- in the Bratunac town? Didn't that seem odd to you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what to say to you. It was as if they were supposed to be put up there, and then when everybody left, then -- well, that's what people were saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody tell you what was going to happen to these people?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. No. Nobody said anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone tell you where they were going to go?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Incidentally, how old were you at the time?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Twenty-one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you said you took the men over there, the able-bodied Muslim men, to the school. Did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We stayed there until about 7.00 or 8.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now, you say "we." Who is "we"?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: We, the military police of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you inside or outside the school?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: We were inside in the school, where we had put up the Muslims, when that unit came, the one that was up there in Potocari. Then at that time, another convoy arrived, a bit bigger, and we left the school, where we had been inside. And then we were deployed from the school towards the main street -- or rather, this big street that went to the main street. I don't know how to explain this to you. I don't know what to say. Actually, it's where the socially-owned bakery was in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That's a side street?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, a side street, about over 100 metres. And that's where the buses were that had come from the direction of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us who it was that ordered you to actually go into the school with the prisoners, you know, these able-bodied men.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: That officer who sent us to the buses to go with them, and he said that we should be there until the soldiers from Potocari came down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And when you got to -- to Bratunac and -- and eventually you said you -- you got outside and you were standing outside the school, was there an officer there that was in charge?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Momir Nikolic came to us then and said, "Be there at the school." So we were there at the school until about 7.00 or 8.00. And then when the convoy came, we went along that street that was lit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But aside from Momir Nikolic, was anybody in charge? Was there a komandir there to make sure that the various people guarding the buses could be placed at various locations?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, there was no one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said at some point you left around 7.00 or 8.00; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: When the convoy came, we were in front of the school, in that street, providing security for the buses that were parked in the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then you indicated that at some point the soldiers from Potocari came; correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those the same soldiers that you indicated with the black uniforms that were doing the separation?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in black uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, where did you spend the night?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: That night the military police had the task to provide security for the buses in that street where the buses were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you stay there the entire night?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The military police stayed there the entire night. But since I had an apartment right there, I went to get a bit of a rest, because I was quite tired by then and I couldn't take it any longer. I went and got some rest, and I joined my colleagues in the morning. I asked my colleagues to let me go and get some rest for a while, and I said, "If anything happens, just call me."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know about what time it was that you went to your apartment to get some rest?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: It was around 10.00, 10.00 or 11.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from where you were standing, could you please tell us how close you were to the stadium that's located in Bratunac town.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: That is very close. It's not even 40 or 50 metres from the bakery to the stadium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We anticipate having a witness coming here at some point testifying that there were some 1.500 Muslim able-bodied men there and that they were being gunned down, executed, by several people. My question is: While you were there on the 13th on that street, some 40 to 50 metres away from the stadium, did you hear executions going on? Bursts of gunfire, as people would be unloading their clips, their entire clips, shooting at masses of people?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, nothing was heard there, not a single bullet was fired when we, the military police, were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you were -- if that had occurred, bursts of gunfire, if that had occurred, do you think it would have been possible for you to have heard it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: How could we not have heard it? I told you, it's about 50 metres. Of course we'd have to hear it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Over the years, have you ever heard of any stories of a large number of Muslims being executed there in the open on that particular night?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not hear any stories in Bratunac that some kind of a massacre had happened or that somebody was killed at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us what you did the next day. You said that you went home, got some rest, and then rejoined your -- your colleagues. What did you do when you got back to that location?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I was there. It was 8.00 or 9.00, and the convoy was getting ready to leave for Zvornik, in the direction of Zvornik. I know that Momir Nikolic himself told me to go up to headquarters, to the military police, to report to Jankovic in order to hear what else we were supposed to do. I went there with another colleague, and Jankovic was by the UNPROFOR APC that was there at our military police headquarters. I saw that he was doing something there, and he was there and I said to him, "Go and get ready. You're supposed to come with me to escort the convoy that was going to Zvornik."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You told him or he told you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I reported to Jankovic, and then he --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He told you to get ready.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm just wondering if we can clarify precisely who the witness is referring to, which Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just for the sake of clarity, for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, for the sake of the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated earlier that your komandir was Jankovic, the commander of the military police; correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mirko Jankovic, the commander of the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the same Mirko Jankovic that you reported to?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Nikolic ordered me to report to Mirko Jankovic up there at the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know by any chance -- you haven't mentioned it, but just in case -- did you know a Colonel Jankovic? Not Mirko, but another, a Colonel Jankovic from the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember that Jankovic. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. All right. So you -- so you reported to Mirko Jankovic. He was at the -- with the white APC, the UN APC. He told you to get ready. What happened then?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Then he drove the APC. We got into the APC. And then we parked by the power supply company in Bratunac. That's where we parked, and we were waiting for this convoy, these buses. We were in the front of the column with this APC.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mirko Jankovic tell you what the mission was?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He said that we were escorting the convoy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you where you were escorting the convoy to?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he didn't tell me where we were escorting the convoy. Later on, when we arrived in Zvornik, it was clear to me that it was Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mirko Jankovic tell you why they were being transported to the Zvornik area?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any idea why they were being taken in that direction?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, where exactly did you and Mirko Jankovic, with the APC, go to?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what the name of the place is, but I can explain which place this was exactly. We passed Zvornik. We came to Karakaj and we passed the flyover, this big flyover. And after the flyover, we went about 50 or 100 metres, and then we turned to the left, an asphalt road too, and then we went for about 2 or 3 kilometres. Then there was a big school there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Had you ever been there before?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you pulled off to the road -- or in -- well, incidentally, let me back up. Was there anyone pointing the direction for Mirko Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was a car in front of the APC.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know who was in the car, who was leading the convoy?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: In that car -- well, the car was a Golf. There were some men in it. I don't know them. I didn't know these men who were in front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated you didn't know them. You didn't recognise them as well?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't recognise them. I didn't know them. They were officers though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But since you didn't recognise them, can we safely assume that they were not officers of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know all the officers of the Bratunac Brigade, because we were there together, the military police and the Bratunac Brigade, and I know all of our officers of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us: When you got to that location when you pulled off the road and you said you went to a -- to where a school was located, what did you see? Please describe that for us.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: While I was going on the APC, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, once you got there -- we'll go back and talk about what you saw on the way, but when you got there, to that location.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When we came to that school, in front of that school there were some soldiers that were waiting for the convoy. There were soldiers that were waiting there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have the same kind of uniforms worn by the Bratunac Brigade soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. They had special ones. There was a unit there that wore these black -- bluish-black overalls, I don't know what to call them, and they wore caps. There were about 30 of them there, and I saw that there were other people there too. I don't know whether they were locals or whatever, but they were all not wearing the same clothing. They were all not wearing the same uniforms. I told you, this unit of about 30 men wore one type of uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, was there someone in charge over there and did you notice if -- if there was a komandant or a komandir in charge?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there was. There was. These men who were in front of us got out of that car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, what was going on when you arrived there? You described who you saw, but could you tell us what, if anything, was happening at the time.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, nothing was happening. We stopped the APC there. We got out of it. Then the Muslim people started getting out too. They were getting off all the buses that were there. There were about two or three soldiers who sat with them on the buses, who were securing the buses. So nothing, they got out, went into the school, and then we stayed there for about 15 minutes to half an hour. We got onto the APC and returned to the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice if there were any abuses going on at the time that you were there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear why the men were being placed in that school, while you were there, that is?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know at that point in time what, if anything, was going to happen to these men?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it not seem strange to you then that once again these men were being transported from one location, one facility, to another facility? Didn't that seem strange to you, albeit you were 21 years old at the time and were with the military police only for a short period of time?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, nothing. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mirko Jankovic, who was a bit more seasoned, did he make any comments as to what he knew or suspected?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's not that we talked that much. In the APC, he was driving and I was sitting way back. We didn't really talk. We didn't make any comments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Incidentally, was there anyone else with you in this APC?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. There were three of us in that vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the third person?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: A colleague, Mile Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said you stayed there for about 15 minutes to a half an hour. While you were there, did you see any executions going on?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any corpses, any dead bodies laying around?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go afterwards?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Back to the military police in Bratunac. We went back there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many trips that day did you make to that location with the APC?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Only one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I would like to spend a few moments with you describing to us what, if anything, you observed on the way from Bratunac to that location, on the way there or on the way back. Did you notice anything unusual on the road?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. In Konjevic Polje, there were our soldiers and we stopped to ask if the road was open, if it was possible to pass through in the direction of Bratunac. They told us it was, and we continued on our way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. When you say "there were our soldiers," are you talking the VRS soldiers or are you saying Bratunac Brigade soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't know those soldiers there in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. There were Serbs -- VRS soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on your way from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje, you have to pass the -- the Kravica agricultural warehouse. So on the way to Konjevic Polje, that would be on your right; on the way back, it would be, again -- no, on your way there, it would be on your left; on your way back, it would be on your right. Did you notice anything unusual as you passed the Kravica agricultural warehouse?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't notice anything. We just passed by along the road and went to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you got to Bratunac, do you know about what time it was?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was just before dark. I don't know what time it was exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what did you do then for the rest of the day? This is July 14th.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: The 14th of July, when we arrived in Bratunac at the military police on the 14th, there were UNPROFOR soldiers there, the ones who had been in Potocari and then they went to the school in Bratunac. And we secured those UNPROFOR soldiers who were put up in the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you do that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't for a long time. They soon left that place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: It was only a few hours that we spent securing them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next day, July 15th, do you recall what you did?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Then we went to Potocari, where UNPROFOR was. That was some sort of -- I don't know what you call it. It was a company, a big company, and in that period there were UNPROFOR soldiers quartered there and we secured their warehouse. There were all sorts of things there, weapons, food, fuel, and we the military police were there securing that warehouse of theirs, and we stayed there six or seven days or five or seven days. I don't know exactly. We were accommodated there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this period, did you ever go to Branjevo Farm, the Branjevo Military Farm?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. I don't even know where that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever go to Pilica and to patrol that area?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the first time that you heard about the Kravica agricultural massacre, if you want to put it that way, the executions that took place in Kravica, in the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the precise date when I heard about it, but it was afterwards, after all these events. I can't remember the exact date. It was seven or ten days later. We were there near Potocari, but no one had ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, we've heard testimony in this court that some 50 bodies were found in that school in Bratunac, the very same school that you had taken the prisoners there on the afternoon of July 13, 1995. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know what happened to the men that you had escorted on that morning of the 14th of July, 1995 as you turned off the road to Zvornik and took them to that school? Do you know what happened to those men?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, but I heard afterwards, about a year later, when television started broadcasting things about this, that they had been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, we started by talking a little bit about Momir Nikolic, and you told us why you believe he provided false testimony under oath about you and the others. Could you please tell us what your relationship was with Momir Nikolic, professionally speaking. Did you get on with the man, as they say?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't get on very well, because after the Srebrenica operation, when we were in Potocari securing UNPROFOR he sent the 15 of us to Trnovo, Treskavica, where the offensive was taking place. He said, "You're going up there as military policemen to be there at the command in Trnovo," and we were to do the job of military policemen. However, when we arrived up there, we spent some three or four days there, and then an order arrived from Momir that we were to go to Treskavica, to Trnovo, up there to the war theatre. We didn't want to go. We refused to obey this order. And then he took offence at this and he came up there and he said to us, "You are not military policemen any more. You're done with the military police." And that's how it was. When we came back, we no longer worked as military policemen, so that we were not on good terms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Petrovic [sic], I want to thank you very much for answering all of my questions. If you could be as frank and forthright with my colleague here, Mr. Stojanovic, or the Prosecution on that end, or the Judges in answering their questions, I would most appreciate it. Thank you again for coming to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions on direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any questions to put to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Mr. Popovic. By your leave, Your Honour, I will ask a few questions in connection with the transfer in the direction of Zvornik. If you agree, we can do this after the break. I don't think I will take more than 10 or 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's almost time for a break, so we'll have the break first and then we'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, your questions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Stojanovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Popovic, I would like to put only a few questions to you about the events of the 14th of July when you set out in the direction of Zvornik. During your examination-in-chief, you said that between 9.00 and 10.00 you began lining up in a column; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the head of a column was an UNPROFOR or UN vehicle.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this vehicle, which was driven by Mirko Jankovic, Mile Petrovic and you were inside; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall approximately when you set out from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: At around 11.00, 11.30, or 12.00. I can't be very precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the distance between Bratunac and the place where you arrived? Or to put it more simply, what is the distance between Bratunac and Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Between Bratunac and Zvornik? I think some 40 to 50 kilometres, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much time did you need to cross that road in that long column?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how long it took, but about an hour and a half or two hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the distance between Zvornik and the school where you arrived approximately?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I can tell you from Karakaj. I don't know how far it is from Zvornik to Karakaj, but after we passed the flyover at Karakaj, we turned left, and then it was about 2 or 2 and a half kilometres down the road, I think. I can't be very precise because I never went there except then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I have added up these hours correctly, may I conclude that you arrived at the school at around 1.30 or 2.00?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: It's possible. I can't tell you very precisely. How should I know? I can just give you my own estimation. I can't tell you precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's try and agree that it was in the afternoon in any case.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible. I can't be precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as I understood it, you did not linger in Zvornik. You continued on toward Karakaj and then turned left. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you joined by the Golf vehicle which was driving in front of the APC?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: It set out from Bratunac with the convoy. I know that when we stopped, they were in front of us, but I can't tell you the name, but I saw a man getting out of the Golf and he said that we should just follow him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I would be correct in saying that along the entire road from Bratunac to that school the Golf vehicle was driving in front of your vehicle?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you reached the school and when the prisoners began to disembark, did they go to the school or to the gym? Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was a gym, but it was a big hall. That's where they went. I could see those big glass windows and it seemed to be some sort of gym. I don't know what the hall was actually used for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the prisoners arrived in that hall, there were no other prisoners there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, Your Honours, could we now go into private session? Because I wish to mention the name of a protected witness. I'd like to check it with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Stojanovic. Any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Your Honours. Thank you. I do have a few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Ms. Issa. Cross-examined by Ms. Issa:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. I just want to go back to when you told us that the duty officer ordered you to go to Potocari on the 13th of July. I just want to clarify, sir: Was that the military police duty officer that you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: The duty officer who was in the military police, he was a policeman but he was on duty, and he told us that we were to go to Potocari, that that's the roster. That was the duty officer who was at the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And perhaps, if I refer you to the military police log, it might refresh your memory as to who that duty officer was. We can perhaps put the 12 and 13 July 1995 on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And that, for the record, is P449, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it says there, sir, that the duty officer was listed as Mile Petrovic on that date. Does that assist you in refreshing your memory as to who it was that ordered you go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, I really can't remember who read out that we should go to Potocari. I was there -- I was new in the police. I didn't know my colleagues well. I really cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine. But you did know Mile Petrovic; right? I think you mentioned him before in the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew Mile Petrovic, but I can't remember for the life of me who it was that read out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fine, sir. Thank you. Did you see any buses -- sorry, could you tell us how many buses went from Potocari to Bratunac carrying the able-bodied men that you've told us about earlier?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: On that day in Potocari, when we, the military police, escorted them to the school down there, I can't tell you exactly, but there were about 15 buses maybe, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they -- the buses contained a large group of men; in other words, could you tell us if the buses were crowded with men? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: The seats were all filled, but they weren't packed with people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you were in Potocari and you saw the men being loaded onto the buses and the women being loaded onto separate buses, did you see anybody kick or hit or abuse any of the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear of anybody getting shot or killed in Potocari, any of the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what the reaction was of the women and children when the men were separated from them?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can describe the reaction. They were miserable. They were crying. It's not easy to leave all that property. I know from my own experience. I lost everything I had, so I know what it was like for them. It wasn't easy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I wasn't referring to the property per se, sir. I was referring to the men being separated from the women and children.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. First the women and children and old men went out, and then the able-bodied military-age men went out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So when the able-bodied men were separated from the rest of the crowd, what was the reaction of the women, children, and the elderly?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: They weren't there at all. They had left earlier. The convoy with the women and children left earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, they were separated from -- the men were separated from the crowd while the women and children were there; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I think that the women and children left before the men left Potocari. First the women, children, and old men left on the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm not talking, sir, about them leaving on the buses. Right now I'm only referring to the actual separations. In order for the women and children to leave on the buses first, the men must have been removed from the crowd. There were no men on the women-and-children buses; isn't that what happened?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't where the separation was up there; I was down by the street. I was securing the street. I wasn't up there where this separation was exactly taking place, and I don't know whether they were all together or whether they were separate, the men and the civilians. I don't know that, in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you see the separations?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, I did not, because I was down there, perhaps about 100 metres away from the place where the separation took place. There's a curve and we just stood by the road, and that's where the Muslim inhabitants passed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see where the men were taken to when they were -- when they were separated or after they were separated?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Afterwards, the men went by us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And were they not placed in a -- in a house nearby, while the operation of removing the women was taking place?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember that. I am telling you I was not there where they were being separated. I was lower down, about 100 metres away, where the buses were. We held that road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, earlier, sir, in your examination-in-chief there was a statement that was referred to that you made to the Bratunac Brigade Military Police -- or sorry, the Bratunac Brigade police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should say the Bratunac police station. I misspoke. Okay, you recall that, sir? And it was given on August 28, 2003; right? Perhaps if we can get you a copy of your statement and you can identify it for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can ask the usher to place the English version on the ELMO. I would ask that we place page 2 on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, before we get to that, if you look at the very end of your statement. I would just ask you to turn to the very last page.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can maybe place the last page on the ELMO as well. Perhaps we can start with that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you made this statement, sir, to the police, was it a truthful statement?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we see here at the --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we see here --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: This is a signature. This is my signature on that statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you signed the statement. And above that, it says that you had an opportunity to read over your statement before you signed it and that you had no objections to it and you had nothing further to add; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you gave the statement, you've told us that it was a truthful one; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we can then, please, turn to page 2 of the statement, have the -- have that pulled up a little bit, please, so we can see the very -- I'd like to see the very bottom of the statement. Thank you. Now, at the very last sentence on that page, sir, after you say that "There were about 10 or 15 of us members to have police there," and you're referring to Potocari, you go on to say, "That same day we were ordered to separate the women, children, and elderly, who according to plan were supposed to be transferred by bus and freight vehicles towards Kladanj." And if we can perhaps just turn to the next page on the ELMO so we can continue along. I'm just reading from the very top of the page. I'm sorry, if you can just move that down so we can see the very top of the page. Thank you. Now, you go on to say, sir, that that -- that you don't know who exactly issued that order; you learned about it from your colleagues. And then you talk about the buses that came from Bratunac, Vihor, the Zvornik-Drina and Srebrenica-Prevoz transportation companies. You describe the women, children, and elderly getting into buses and trucks, and then you continue on and you say, "After a convoy was formed, they were taken in the direction of the Bratunac and further on towards Kladanj. That same afternoon, the rest of the people from the group who were primarily able-bodied men were transferred by buses and trucks from Potocari to Bratunac." So according to your statement, sir, it appears that the military police were ordered to separate the women and children from the men. Isn't that what happened?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, that's not what happened. This is the statement I made, that we were in Potocari in that place, but that's not really what we did. We held the road. We secured the road, and Muslims came down to that road, to those buses. It's about 100 kilometres [as interpreted] away. That's the statement I made. We were not there on the actual site that -- and it was not that we were doing the actual separation. That was not our task. The statement that I gave was that we were there in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, in -- in the transcript, there should be 100 metres away, rather than 100 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, just to clarify for the record, how far away you were.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I was or we were away from that place where the separation took place. Down to the buses it was about, say, 100 metres. I can't tell you exactly, but say 100.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for pointing that out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've already told us that you had -- that there were about 15 buses with men that you and your colleagues escorted to Bratunac. Can you tell us whether the Muslim men had their belongings with them when they were escorted to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, they didn't have anything on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to their belongings?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't think that was unusual?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. They didn't have anything on them. Perhaps somebody had a bag of food or something, but it's not that they had any big bags or something like that. I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that you -- they were escorted to a school. And I just want to clarify. Was that the Vuk Karadzic School that they were escorted to?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I think that that school changed its name now. Now it's Vuk Karadzic, but at that time I think it was Branko Radicevic, the school that they were put up in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to clarify that that's the same school that we were referring to, that we know as Vuk Karadzic -- Karadzic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you were there, you said that there were other Bratunac Brigade military police with you that were at one point securing the school, securing the Muslims in the school; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any other Bratunac Brigade soldiers, regular soldiers at the school?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. No. It was only us, the military police. We were securing the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any other military police that you did not know?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Afterwards, before it got dark, the corps police came and they were there after 8.00 or 9.00 in the evening, later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And were they -- what were they doing there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what they were doing. At any rate, they came in the escort. I mean, when those buses came from the stadium. I saw them walking around, and I saw the words "Corps police of Republika Srpska" written.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they guarding the Muslims in the school or on the buses?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: In the school, it was the special police that was guarding them. We were there until the evening, 6.00 or 7.00 in the evening. I don't know the exact hour. And then they came to the school. Because there wasn't any electricity at the school or anything. We went out, and they came to the school, and then we went from the school to this street towards the main street. I don't know the exact name of the street. But it's not the centre. It's from the school towards the main street, where the bakery is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're saying that you left the school at about 6.00 or 7.00 in the evening.; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The military police left the school, and these people, these -- this special unit came to that school, and we were transferred to this street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say "we, the military police," just for clarification, you're --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: The military police, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're referring to the Bratunac Brigade Military Police; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to go to your -- to your statement, if I can just get the assistance of Mr. Usher. I'd ask that we turn to page 3, both in the B/C/S version and in the English translation. Thank you. And if we can perhaps start from the middle of the page, around -- around line 15 or perhaps even a little bit earlier than that. You say: "The Muslim citizens who were brought in were put up in what is today the Branko Radicevic elementary school, that is, in the sports hall and throughout the school. The other members of the military police and I - there were around 10 of us - stayed to secure the elementary school, or rather, the prisoners until the following day." It appears to -- that you're saying there, sir, in your statement that you gave to the Bratunac police, that you were at the school until the following day.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The military police was there until the following day; that is to say, we were there all night from the school towards that street, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, with all due respect, you don't say "towards that street." You say that you stayed to secure the school, "or rather, the prisoners until the following day." That's different than saying that you left around 6.00 or 7.00 at night towards the street, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But we were securing that school already when the next convoy came. When they came, then we were transferred to this street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's no reference in the statement here, sir, that you were transferred to a street, is there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, all right. I mean, that -- that street is right by the school, so I mean, had I known the number of the street or the name of the street, I would have said we were in such-and-such a street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's no -- there doesn't say anything about anybody else coming there to the school, does it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it doesn't say anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, earlier you told us that you saw the corps police, and I -- and what I'd like to clarify is whether you saw them guarding the buses on the street. Can you tell us whether they were doing that or not?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. They were not guarding them. That's what we, the military police, did. They just went by, I don't know where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And this is on the evening of the 13th of July, right, just -- just to be clear?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes, on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there prisoners in the hangar behind the school?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much buses -- I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I mean, the entire school is all linked up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So when you say it's "all linked up," is the school linked up to the hangar behind the school? Like a warehouse?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, it's separate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there prisoners in that location?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were. But later on they were transferred to the upper storey of the school. The school had a ground floor and an upper storey, so later on they were transferred upstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're saying that the -- there were prisoners in the hangar behind the school and they were subsequently transferred to the upper floor of the Vuk Karadzic School; is that -- is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think they were transferred there because both the ground floor and the upper floor were full.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were full of prisoners; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And who was guarding the prisoners in the hangar behind the school?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know who guarded them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then who moved them from the hangar to the upper floor of the Vuk Karadzic School?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: That police, when they came, this special police. They came with them and they escorted them all the way upstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Were there prisoners in the engineering school nearby?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. I didn't hear about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would be the other school that was next to the hangar?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many buses were there outside the school containing prisoners?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: From --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm sorry. Outside the Vuk Karadzic School.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: There weren't any buses behind the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Were there buses in front of the school?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: In front of the Vuk Karadzic School, yes, in that street that I told you about a short while ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And there were men, Muslim men, prisoners that were on those buses; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you told us that the Bratunac Brigade Military Police were guarding those men on the buses?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there, sir, did you hear or see any of the men being beaten, kicked, or abused in any way?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anyone getting shot?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear that. At 10.00 or 11.00 I went to get a bit of a rest, and then in the morning I joined my colleagues. I didn't hear anything or ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the wounded men, either in the school or on the buses, receive medical attention?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there weren't any wounded. There was no one on the buses who was wounded. They asked us for water, and there was a fountain there, and we poured some water for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know, there were several people who testified or said that -- who survived who said that there were men that were removed from the -- from the buses and trucks and who were beaten and then shot. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, these buses, they were lined up all the way to the soccer stadium?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: We were guarding them from the school towards this street that I talked about a few minutes ago. So there's the school, and then the street goes straight ahead from there, and that's where the bakery is too. That's where the military police was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And this soccer stadium, it has a big wall around it, doesn't it, that's about 2 metres high; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see prisoners being removed from the buses and taken to the stadium?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were aware that there were prisoners inside the stadium; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, you do say in your statement to the Bratunac police - we can maybe turn to page 4, if I can just have the assistance of Mr. Usher, thank you - at just about the middle of the page you say: "During this period, I learned that there was a group of prisoners who was also present at the town stadium in Bratunac on the same day when we transferred the prisoners from Potocari." And you go on to say that you didn't go to the stadium and you don't know what happened there. So there were prisoners in the -- in the stadium. You're referring to the soccer stadium there, when you talk about "the stadium" in your statement; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the soccer stadium. But this group that was at the stadium, it was not from Potocari; it came from the direction of Konjevic Polje, from down there. Because the people who were at the school were from Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
