utterances.text: So you saw the -- they were men that were bussed from the direction of Konjevic Polje and brought to the soccer stadium?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us who was escorting them to the soccer stadium?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, I can't say that, because I didn't see who escorted them, nor do I know this. All I know is that they came to the stadium from that direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I just want to ask you a few questions about the events when you escorted the convoy, the men from the schools to Zvornik. Can you tell us who was on the buses guarding the men while they were being escorted to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That special unit that was there in that school. I don't know exactly. I went two or three hours or 2.00 or 3.00, and the convoy went -- I went to report. But the special police who were there, they went with them, with the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: From the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what school did they arrive at in Zvornik? Can you describe that school?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I can describe it, but I don't know the name of the place exactly. It's a village. We passed by Zvornik. Then there was Karakaj, and then there was a flyover, a big flyover. You pass that, and then just 50 or 100 metres down the road there's a turning to the left. It's an asphalt road. And it leads straight to the school, to that village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many vehicles were in the column?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how many, but it was a really long column, about 1 or 2 kilometres long. I know when we were starting out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us who went to -- who went up to Pilica?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: To Pilica? No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we can then turn to the military police log.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can ask Mr. Usher's assistance. I'll be referring to 19 July. For the record, Your Honour, that's Exhibit P449.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, that -- just for the record, it says up there no date, but that's in between -- between the 18th and the 20th. Now, we see there, sir, that it refers to "Patrols went to secure the public utility workers in Glogova." Were you aware that public utility workers were securing -- patrols were securing the public utility workers in Glogova on that day?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, our military police went to secure the people who were digging.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were digging mass graves in Glogova; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No. It wasn't our military police who were digging. They were just providing security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. They were providing security for the people who were digging the mass graves; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those mass graves were of the people who were killed at Kravica; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. I don't know where they were killed, how this came about. I just know that two or three policemen went to secure them. That's what I heard while we were in Potocari, that some colleagues went to secure those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you hear? What were they digging? The public utility workers, that is.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what they were digging. Our patrol went to provide security for those. How should I know?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You weren't aware, sir, that there were mass graves that were dug in Glogova that contained hundreds of bodies of Muslim men during that period?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of it at the time, but I did hear about it later on, that that happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you hear about it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, afterwards, it was autumn. I don't know what month exactly, but it was three or four months later that I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I heard that there was a mass grave there and that from Glogova it was driven off. I don't know. That's all I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that autumn time period, sir, did you hear that the mass grave was -- they were dug up and that the bodies were reburied, were moved and reburied? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. People were saying that that mass grave had been removed, taken away from that place in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "people were saying," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when you sit down with someone, they would say a mass grave was found as Glogova and it was moved. Nobody came and said to me, "Listen, this and that was found."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But this was common knowledge, in other words? People knew that this mass grave was moved, say, around October of 1995? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I wasn't there. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you also said that you apparently heard about the Kravica warehouse killings later. I think you said you heard about this seven or ten days later in your examination-in-chief. How did you hear about this?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in the same way. It was hearsay. I didn't see it with my own eyes. I just heard people saying that something had happened in Kravica. I hadn't been there. I do come from Kravica, but it was only in the winter that I went home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is just something that people were talking, again. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, people were talking about it. I don't know that this happened in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Issa. Any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have a few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please. Re-examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On May 6, 2003, a cooperating witness for the Prosecution came and gave a statement accusing you of being involved in the killings in Kravica. Here we are now, 2004, at the end of June or near the end of June. Did the Prosecution ever visit you to see whether the information that Momir Nikolic had given to them was true?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't see how this arises out of the cross-examination. He certainly could have asked these questions in chief. And if phrased differently, it's also quite leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that redirect examination should be strictly within the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's with -- I'll rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You then gave a statement on the 28th of August, 2003. And my question is, going back to my previous question, in light of the fact that the Prosecutor is asking you all of this detailed information, had they wished to come and visit you in Bratunac, had they been interested in what you had to say, were you available to provide them the same information in greater detail that you provided the Bratunac police back on August 28, 2003? Were you available for them had they wanted to know all of these details?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is clearly a speech. It doesn't arise out of the cross-examination. It appears that Mr. Karnavas is just arguing and testifying in his usual way. It's totally improper.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think your question could be put in a very simple way, you know, rather than bring the Prosecution into the picture, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I believe, Your Honour, what I heard was not "cross-examination" but was direct examination, as if they're trying to investigate through the trial, and I was just wondering, since they were interested in all of these details and they're trying to assume that the gentleman was untruthful or less than --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, I'm going to have to object to the -- in front of the witness going on and on and making these arguments. It's -- it's inappropriate. If Mr. Karnavas wants to question the Prosecution about our investigation, he is -- he is welcome to. But this witness is not a -- the place for a speech.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Prosecution ever come to you to meet with you to question you about their statement that would have been ready available to them all the various trips they made to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is contemptuous conduct. He is deliberately ignore the Court's instructions and it demeans the entire process. It needs to be stopped, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't understand. We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes, Mr. Karnavas. I think the first part of your question is okay. You just put your question there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And I believe that we gave you on many occasions the instructions. I just hope you to follow it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I've been following the instructions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We received this -- this statement of yours from the Bratunac police on -- that you gave August 28th, 2003. Had the Prosecution wanted to question you about what you told the police, would you have been willing to meet with them?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you think of any reason why the Prosecution would not come and meet with you, given that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- given that Momir Nikolic accused him or --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're just -- he needs to be stopped. This is contemptuous of the Court. It's deliberately flouting the Court. If we can't get any organisation, this is complete anarchy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: This question is not proper to put to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, he was accused of killing people or being involved in massacres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The Prosecution brought their witness, their star witness, and made that accusation. One would think that the Prosecution would at least meet with the gentleman. And I'm asking him if he has any reasons why they didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think this question should be put to the Prosecution on other occasions, not to the witness. How could you ask this witness to speculate?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, perhaps he was out of -- out of town or out of the country.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I don't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic? Any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only one question, Your Honour. The witness and I were both listening to the interpretation, and I was waiting for it to finish. Further cross-examination by Mr. Stojanovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Today during your cross-examination you were asked where you arrived in Zvornik, in the Zvornik municipality, what place. Can you recall in accordance with what you learned later about what happened to these people that the name of the place was Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: No, I can't recall that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one more question: You said that when you passed the flyover, you turned off left toward the school. Now, try to recall whether the school was to the left or to the right-hand side looking in the direction of Tuzla. To the left or to the right of the road?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA POPOVIC
utterances.text: To the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at this stage are there any documents to tender? Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're willing to tender D205, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections, Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, since there's no objections from the Prosecution, this document is admitted into the evidence. But generally speaking, I'd be very reluctant to admit this document into evidence, you know. This is one of the previous statements, and it is extensively used in the proceedings, everything in the transcript. But since, since there is no objections and the Defence tendered this document, we admitted it into the evidence. And are there any documents to tender on the part of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I don't have any documents to tender. And I just wanted to point out that aside from not making any objection to this document, we actually encourage the use of the document by the Court. We think that it's -- it would be quite useful in the determination of the credibility of -- of the evidence overall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. We wish you a pleasant journey back home. The usher will show you out of the courtroom. You may go now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, tomorrow we will have another witness. We'll start from 9.00 in the morning and we will have an extra session in the afternoon, as well as on Friday. The time for the afternoon session will be 3.00 to 4.30, which is one hour and a half, and we hope we could finish the testimony of that witness in this week. I'm a little bit worried about the performance by the parties, especially concerning with tomorrow's witness. I believe that I have to remind the parties for several things: I think I have to reiterate our concern and warnings to the parties. This is a Tribunal but not a truth and reconciliation committee. The purpose of this Tribunal is to see whether the accused is innocent or not in that incident. So I hope the questions put to the witness should be strictly limited within the scope of the purpose of this Tribunal. I would not like to see any proliferations of the questions. The Srebrenica massacre is a very big issue. Many questions should be answered by historians rather than by this Tribunal. We only have a limited mandate for this Tribunal. The second issue is about -- I hope during the direct examination, as well as cross-examination and re-examination, the parties should show respect to the witness and to their counterparts, their colleagues in this courtroom. Frankly speaking, this Bench was not satisfied with the behaviour of the parties. I hope the parties should bear in mind the warnings from this Bench and should behave themselves in this courtroom. This is just a warning, but if we see that things happen again and again, we are going to take some measures to stop it. Well, that's all I have to say at this stage. And are there any matters that the parties would like to bring to the attention of this Bench? Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. Karnavas and I have spoken briefly about the 92 bis witnesses, and there was some discussion about a second review. But with -- given the Court's allowing just this one witness, that I think -- in that case, I think that one witness should -- should come to testify. I haven't had a chance to tell that to Mr. Karnavas, but we had been talking about it. We do speak to each other. We will continue to speak to each other. And I just wanted you to know that, and -- but just for scheduling, there's -- that one witness - I can't recall exactly his name - but there is one -- I think it's another -- I think it's an MP, as a matter of fact. We would like it if we could hear for a -- for cross-examination under 92 bis. The other question is: I know Mr. Karnavas was going to report back to us to see if he's heard any word from Serbia on the waiver issues. I -- that is an important issue for the Office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We actually speak to each other and with each other. First of all, with the one witness for next week: We immediately, as soon as we got the Court's -- the Court's order, we immediately made contact with the witness. They needed to get a -- a passport, and everything is underway. I don't know the exact date. It would -- my preference would be to handle him on Monday, if everything could be arranged, but I don't know if that's possible before Tuesday or Wednesday, but I will keep everybody updated. So that's that issue. And I don't think -- frankly, I don't see the reason why we need to bring him, but I'm always willing to bring witnesses here. With respect to the waiver issue, with the first gentleman, as I understand it, we should be getting it any moment; with the second gentleman, if we -- if everybody recollects who that gentleman was, as far as I understand, after leaving The Hague and being subpoenaed or summoned -- I should say summoned, as he was about to check into the airport, the gentleman went -- complained to the commission of the way he was treated. We've contacted the commission. We've tried to inform them that, you know, there are reasons why OTP wanted to question him. Perhaps their tactic could have been a little different, you know, but that's the way things work. But with that particular gentleman, I am -- I am very doubtful that we're going to get anything, and I've even made the request of a simple letter -- a simple letter, something. So I will keep working on that. And I know that Ms. Tomanovic is going into the field and will be stopping in Belgrade and will personally look into the matter. But that's all I have. But with the first gentleman, I believe all the paperwork is being done, it's on its way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much for -- for the information you provided us. And I think you mentioned that you see no need to question that witness -- I mean, the 92 bis witness, which means that you've waived your right to direct examine this witness. Could I understand it in this way?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, once a witness steps into the courtroom, I'm always delighted to have the opportunity to question the witness. I think the -- the questioning wouldn't take more than a half an hour. The reason I said what I said earlier was we've already had two such MPs that were part of the -- General Mladic's entourage that went from Bratunac, stopped in Sandici, Vlasenica, and so on and so forth. That's why I didn't see the need to bring in a third person. And as you may recall, I had him originally on my list and then took him off as a result of the Trial Chamber's guidance that we received at one of the hearings. That's why I was saying that I don't see what more we can get out of it. It's the same story. But since he will be here, I might as well avail myself to the opportunity to do a brief direct, point him in the right direction. But, of course, if the Trial Chamber does not wish me to do that, then I guess I'll have to do my questioning on redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that witness is a 92 bis witness. The statement will eventually be admitted into evidence. So on the part of this Bench, we see no necessity for the direct examination. But -- but you promised us that you have a very brief direct, and that could be allowed. MR. KARNAVAS: Brief. I don't know very, but brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Brief. Yes, brief. I think you really just draw the highlights

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. JUDGE LIU: -- of his, you know, testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Rather than go into the specific details, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will do that. JUDGE LIU: Thank you very much. Well, having said that, I think the hearing for today is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 24th day of June, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.00 p.m.,
